journey.title: Escape must not dismiss a dialog opened with keyboard: false
journey.goal: The confirmation dialog stays open however often Escape is pressed, so the user can still enter the code and send the transfer

functionalJourney.title: Confirm with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking the backdrop does not close the dialog; entering the code and clicking Send completes the transfer

guards.title: Cancel transfer still closes the dialog from the keyboard
guards.goal: Tabbing to Cancel transfer and pressing Enter closes the dialog and records the cancellation

guards.title: Escape still closes a dialog with the default options
guards.goal: An ordinary dialog created without options opens with Enter and closes with Escape

plan.root_cause: The cancel listener for the native Escape key is bound without a namespace, making it vulnerable to being removed by generic EventHandler.off calls elsewhere in the codebase. After two Escape presses, something (likely internal cleanup) unbinds the listener, causing the third Escape to trigger the dialog's default close action.
plan.repair_strategy: Replace the raw 'cancel' event strings with the namespaced EVENT_CANCEL constant when attaching and detaching the native cancel listener in DialogBase, ensuring the listener is uniquely scoped and not inadvertently removed by other code.

edits.before:
// The `cancel` listener is unnamespaced, so super.dispose()'s EVENT_KEY\n    // teardown misses it — remove this instance's own handler here.
    EventHandler.off(this._element, 'cancel', this._cancelHandler)
edits.after:
// The `cancel` listener is namespaced, so super.dispose()'s EVENT_KEY\n    // teardown will remove it — remove this instance's own handler here.
    EventHandler.off(this._element, EVENT_CANCEL, this._cancelHandler)

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will no longer dismiss the confirmation dialog when it is initialized with keyboard: false, allowing users to repeatedly press Escape to dismiss transient warnings or refocus without losing the OTP input field.
functional_risks: If other code intentionally relies on unbinding the raw 'cancel' listener to suppress Escape behavior, those callers will no longer affect the dialog.
Changing the event name may interfere with any external listeners that expect the bare 'cancel' event (though such usage is non-standard and discouraged).
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape any number of times while the confirmation dialog is open does not close the dialog when keyboard: false and backdrop: static.
Verify that pressing Escape still closes non‑modal dialogs and modal dialogs with keyboard: true.
Ensure that the backdrop 'static' bounce effect still occurs on Escape when keyboard: false.
Confirm that disposing the dialog properly removes the namespaced listener.
Check that no JavaScript errors are introduced in the event‑handling flow.

plan.root_cause: The `_onCancel` method in `dialog-base.ts` references an undefined constant `EVENT_CANCEL`. This causes a runtime error (`EVENT_CANCEL is not defined`) when the method is called, breaking Escape key handling and dialog dismissal logic. The constant is defined in the child class `dialog.ts` but not in the base class, so any direct use of `DialogBase` or scenarios where the base implementation is invoked will fail.
plan.repair_strategy: Replace the undefined `EVENT_CANCEL` constant with a dynamic lookup using the existing `eventName` static method from `BaseComponent`. This ensures the correct namespaced event name is used for any subclass (including `DialogBase` itself) without introducing new constants.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will no longer throw a JavaScript error when the dialog's `_onCancel` hook runs. This restores the intended behavior: for dialogs with `keyboard: false` the Escape key triggers only the backdrop bounce (via `_triggerBackdropTransition`) and does not dismiss the dialog, while for dialogs with `keyboard: true` the dialog closes normally. The confirmation dialog (keyboard: false, backdrop: static) will stay open regardless of how many times Escape is pressed, allowing the user to enter the OTP and complete the transfer.
functional_risks: If any external code relies on the base class's `_onCancel` triggering a specific event name other than the standard namespaced `cancel.bs.dialog`, that coupling will change. However, the standard event name is exactly what `eventName('cancel')` returns for the `Dialog` class, so normal Bootstrap usage is unaffected.
verification_requirements: Verify that the confirmation dialog (keyboard: false, backdrop: static) does not close when Escape is pressed any number of times.
Verify that the help dialog (default options) still closes when Escape is pressed.
Verify that the cancel button (`#cancel-transfer`) still closes the confirmation dialog via keyboard (Tab + Enter).
Verify that no `EVENT_CANCEL is not defined` errors appear in the console.
Verify that the OTP input receives focus after the confirmation dialog opens (initial focus restoration).
